cards.text: Right before this, enemy horses are heard snorting from Dan, and the whole land quakes. Now Jeremiah, God's prophet, speaks, and friend, he is hurting. He says, 'My sorrow is beyond healing; my heart is faint within me.'

cards.question: The prophet says to listen to a cry from the daughter of his people, coming from a land far away. What are they asking?

answers.text: Whether the LORD is still in Zion
Whether Egypt will send them help
Whether the rain will ever return

cards.text: And right in the middle of their cry, the LORD speaks up with a question of His own.

cards.question: The LORD asks why His people have provoked Him to anger, and His question points straight at their ___.
The people's cry goes on: the harvest has passed and the summer has ended. True or false: they say they have finally been saved.

cards.text: Harvest gone, summer gone, still not saved, like waiting all day for the repair guy and the window closes and NOBODY ever knocks. And the prophet says, 'For the brokenness of the daughter of my people I am crushed.'

cards.question: Then the prophet asks, 'Is there no balm in Gilead? Is no physician there?' What is he really asking?

answers.text: Why his people still aren't healed
Where to find medicine for himself
When Gilead will send its army

cards.text: Then the prophet wishes his head were a spring of water and his eyes a fountain of tears, and he says he would weep day and night over the slain daughter of his people. Friend, he's not reaching for a tissue here, he wants a whole FOUNTAIN.

cards.question: Right after all those tears, the prophet makes a wish about the wilderness. What does he wish he had out there?

answers.text: A traveler's lodge to leave his people
A quiet place to pray for his people
A well to bring his people water

cards.question: Why does the prophet say he would leave his own people behind?

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks. He says, 'They bend their tongues like bows; lies prevail over truth in the land.'

cards.question: With lies everywhere in the land, what does the LORD tell everyone to do about his neighbor?
True or false: the LORD says a brother can still be trusted, even if a neighbor can't.

cards.text: They've taught their tongues to lie, and they wear themselves out committing iniquity. Friend, that's working OVERTIME at the wrong job.

cards.question: The LORD says, 'You dwell in the midst of deception.' Then He says the deceivers refuse to do something. What is it?

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says what He will do, and He asks what else He can do, because of the daughter of His people. I think that question hits different, friend, when it's coming from the LORD of Hosts Himself.

cards.question: So what does the LORD of Hosts say He will do to His people?

answers.text: Give them a brand new king

cards.text: The LORD says their tongues are deadly arrows, and they speak deception. So those tongues bent like bows earlier, friend, now we know what they're FIRING.

cards.question: The LORD describes a two-faced man: with his ___ he speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his ___ he sets a trap for him.
True or false: after all this, the LORD says He will simply overlook what this nation has done.

cards.text: Then a weeping and wailing goes up for the mountains, a dirge over the wilderness pasture. Friend, when the MOUNTAINS get their own sad song, you know something has gone real wrong out there.

cards.question: Why is there wailing over the mountains and the wilderness pasture?

answers.text: They've been scorched and left empty
A great flood has covered them
Strangers have fenced them all off

cards.question: True or false: out on that scorched land, even the birds of the air and the beasts have fled.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, 'And I will make Jerusalem a heap of rubble, a haunt for jackals; and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.'

findings.problem: The card tells Jeremiah 9:8 but also retells the earlier image of tongues bent like bows from Jeremiah 9:3. Citing only Jeremiah 9:8 is narrower than the verses the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The two blanks reproduce the line from Jeremiah 9:8 and ask for its unseen wording, 'mouth' and 'heart.' This tests the words of the line rather than its movement or meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
